To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the aortic calibres of conscious rats were chronically monitored by a new technique; 2) during the onset of aortic constriction-induced acute hypertension, the dilation of the aorta was greater during the first 6 h than during the following 48 h; and 3) the dilation was greater during the diastolic phase than during the systolic phase.

1) the dilation of the aortic calibres during acute hypertension is a slow process, 2) the dilation of aortic calibra is not a passive process, and 3) the time course for the dilation of the diastole is similar to the time course for resetting of the afferent baroreceptor activity.
the time course for the resetting of baroreceptors is coincident with the time course of the dilation of the aorta in acute hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the time course of resetting of the aorta baroreflex in hypertension.
the time course of dilation of the aorta in acute hypertension and its relation to baroreceptor resetting.
the time course of the aortic calibral changes during the onset of hypertension and the role of the diastole for the baroreceptor resetting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aortic baroceptors reset to a new equilibrium when the time course of dilation of the aortic calibres is completed.
the resetting of aortic baroreflexes in acute hypertension depends on the time taken for aortic dilation to achieve a new equilibrium.
the time course for the resetting of aortic baroreflexes is related to the time required for the aorta in acute hypertension to achieve a new resting diastolic calibrational equilibrium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time taken for the aorta and its receptors to achieve a new equilibrium state in hypertension is determined by the time taken to increase the aortic diastole.
a new state of equilibrium in the aortic wall is necessary for complete resetting of baroreceptor sensitivity in hypertension.
aortic baroreceptor resetting is a function of the dilation of the aortic diastole and not of aortic pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aortic baroreceptor resetting is not a passive process, but is dependent on the time course of dilation of the aorta during the establishment of a new level of arterial pressure, and that the time course of resetting of aortic baroreflexes is dependent upon aortic distensibility.
in the rat, the aortic baro-receptors do not reset until the time that the aortic diastole is maximally dilated.
aortic baroreceptor resetting is not only dependent on the level of hypertension but also on the time course of the aortic dilation.
